section_summary: This section concerns the Parker Pen Company’s request for U.S. diplomatic help with Japanese patent and trademark decisions. The U.S. Commissioner of Patents found no evidence of discrimination, while the State and Commerce Departments discussed whether there was another basis for approaching Japan. Most of the section is Parker’s petition and technical exhibits concerning its fountain pen filling device.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department letter on Parker Pen Company difficulties in Japan
subfiles.from: Lacey C. Zapf, Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.to: Wilbur J. Carr, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests assistance with Parker’s Japanese patent and trademark difficulties despite the Patent Office’s adverse assessment.
subfiles.summary: Zapf forwards the Commissioner of Patents’ letter and Parker’s memoranda and exhibits. He argues that Japanese decisions and imitations damage Parker’s trade in Japan and other markets.

subfiles.title: Commissioner of Patents’ assessment of Parker’s complaints
subfiles.about: Finds no evidence that Japan’s patent and trademark decisions discriminated against Parker as a U.S. company.
subfiles.summary: The Commissioner reviews two patent matters and the Park and Park Minor trademark dispute. He says differing patent judgments do not establish treaty violations, one opposition remains pending, and Parker failed to appeal one refusal.
keywords: International Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property

subfiles.title: State Department reply concerning Parker’s proposed protest
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Asks Commerce to identify a reasonable basis for raising Parker’s complaints with Japan.
subfiles.summary: The State Department recounts its earlier willingness to consider diplomatic action if U.S. technical authorities supported Parker’s petitions. Quoting the Commissioner’s contrary findings, it asks Commerce to explain the claimed intangible barriers to American firms and to identify a practical basis for approaching Japan.

subfiles.title: Draper’s acknowledgment of State Department reply
subfiles.from: Ernest G. Draper, Assistant Secretary of Commerce
subfiles.about: Promises further study of grounds for presenting Parker’s complaints to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Draper acknowledges State’s reply and says Commerce will study the matter further.

subfiles.title: Handwritten annotation
subfiles.about: A largely illegible handwritten page precedes Parker’s petition.
subfiles.summary: The OCR yields only a brief, uncertain annotation.

subfiles.title: Parker petition concerning Japanese patent application and utility model
subfiles.about: Seeks intervention over Japanese handling of Parker’s fountain pen filling device.
subfiles.summary: Parker traces its Japanese patent application through successive citations, rejection, and conversion to a utility model application. Although the utility model was accepted, Shuichi Sasaki opposed registration. Parker contrasts Japanese delay with grants elsewhere and says Japanese copies are harming its international sales.

subfiles.title: U.S. Patent 1,980,508, Fountain Pen Filling Device
subfiles.from: Ivan D. Tefft, assignor to the Parker Pen Company
subfiles.about: Describes and claims Tefft’s diaphragm and plunger fountain pen filling mechanism.
subfiles.summary: The patent includes drawings, a technical description, operation and assembly instructions, and sixteen claims. Its device uses a flexible diaphragm, spring loaded plunger, locking mechanism, and removable filling unit.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-I: Japanese patent application specification and claims, Case 7
subfiles.about: Sets out Parker’s Japanese application for its fountain pen filling device.
subfiles.summary: The specification describes the diaphragm, plunger, spring, locking pin, assembly, and operation of the filling device. Four claims seek protection for the mechanism and its locking features. Parker’s petition states that these papers were filed in Japan on September 6, 1933.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-II: First Japanese bureau notice for application 9319
subfiles.about: Cites Japanese Utility Model 35069 against Parker’s application.
subfiles.summary: The examiner treats Parker’s differences as routine mechanical design.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-III: Japanese Utility Model 35069
subfiles.about: Reproduces the Japanese utility model first cited against Parker’s application.
subfiles.summary: The exhibit contains Japanese text and drawings for Utility Model 35069, which Parker disputed as a relevant prior disclosure.

subfiles.title: Patent specification excerpt on a diaphragm fountain pen filler
subfiles.about: Provides a technical excerpt describing a diaphragm and plunger filling device.
subfiles.summary: A reproduced patent page describes diaphragm mounting, plunger parts, and filling operation.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-IV: Instructions on first Japanese patent objection
subfiles.about: Instructs Parker’s Japanese representative to distinguish its diaphragm filler from Utility Model 35069.
subfiles.summary: The letter identifies leakage problems in the cited plunger design and proposes amended claims emphasizing Parker’s sealed diaphragm and plunger lock.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-V: Supplemental instructions on Japanese patent claims
subfiles.about: Supplies U.S.-allowed claims and further arguments for Parker’s Japanese application.
subfiles.summary: Parker explains why its spring, diaphragm, and lock differ from the cited Japanese plunger design and asks that at least some claim be allowed.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-VI: Subsequent bureau notice for application 9319
subfiles.about: Cites Utility Model Publication 25175 and Registration 64072 against Parker’s application.
subfiles.summary: The examiner considers Parker’s diaphragm and spring an obvious combination of known features.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-VII: Japanese Utility Model Publication 25175
subfiles.about: Reproduces a cited Japanese fountain pen utility model publication.
subfiles.summary: Japanese text and a drawing show the prior model cited against Parker.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-VIII: Parker’s response instructions on cited utility models
subfiles.about: Details arguments against the Japanese examiner’s utility model citations.
subfiles.summary: Parker explains the spring released diaphragm filler, its seal, and its locking and assembly features. It argues that the cited plunger models lack these features or risk ink leakage, and urges de Havilland to contest rejection.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-IX: Rejection of application 9319
subfiles.about: Rejects Parker’s application as lacking inventive novelty.
subfiles.summary: The examiner finds the diaphragm, spring, and plunger lock derivable from known designs.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-X: Bureau notice for utility model application 10637
subfiles.about: Requests narrower claims, a shorter specification, and changes to drawings.
subfiles.summary: The examiner asks Parker to explain differences from prior citations and cancel Figure 2.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A-XI: Instructions on utility model application 10637
subfiles.about: Directs Parker’s representative how to amend and defend the utility model application.
subfiles.summary: Parker emphasizes the plunger safety lock, diaphragm attachment, and unit assembly as its distinctive features. It disputes the cited models and suggests shortening portions of the specification while retaining the drawing that shows the diaphragm clamp.
